title: Give the art pipeline a palette-collapse step, and audit the loose sprites
tier_reason: The pipeline step is pure automation; the retroactive pass touches shipped art, so its output goes to Daniel as before/after contact sheets rather than landing directly.
ask:
Daniel noticed the songbird carries ~30 distinct colors in 234 opaque pixels (9 colors used by a single pixel) — generator anti-aliasing that was never collapsed. The disciplined sprites show the target: chicken 7 colors, crow 5, wheat 8. The rabbit (21) is also loose. The pipeline's postprocess (~/.claude/skills/retro-diffusion-pixel-art/scripts/postprocess.py) has key_background/trim/fit_cell but no palette quantization step at all.

Two parts:
1. Add a quantize_palette step to the pipeline's post-processing: weighted k-means (or median-cut) over the sprite's own opaque colors with distance measured in OKLab, snapping each pixel to the nearest of the N surviving colors, where each palette entry is a real color from the image (never an invented average), no dithering at 16px. Default N by sprite size (~8-12 for 16px cells). Run it on every future generation after background keying.
2. Audit every sheet in assets/sprites/generated/ for color count; for the loose ones, produce before/after contact sheets at 2-3 candidate palette sizes (a 2026-09-06 chat demo did this for the songbird at 16/12/8/6 — at 8 the sprite reads identically) and bring them to Daniel for the pick. Do not land quantized art without his eye — this is a look call.

Note: work item we7a0d7228ec (the key_background fringe fix, written but unapplied because the skill lives outside the repo) touches the same file — coordinate so the two postprocess changes land together, and know that some of the singleton colors in the audit are that fringe.
